title: Duality against pullback
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, with $\ell\ne p$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ as there. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes (the domain of the absolute dualizing objects in [def-sf-pf]), and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism. Write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and $D_T=R\mathcal H om_T(-,Ra_T^!\Lambda)$ for $T=X,Y$, using the completed integral and common-stage field conventions of the datum. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$
\chi_f:D_XLf^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!D_Y
$$
of contravariant functors, that is, of functors $\mathcal C_Y^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C_X$. It is natural in $f$: it is the identity for $f=\mathrm{id}$ under the unit identifications, and for composable separated finite-type morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ it obeys
$$
\chi_{gf,B}=Rf^!(\chi_{g,B})\circ\chi_{f,Lg^*B}
$$
under the pullback and exceptional-composition identifications. If an orientation datum [def-sf-orientation] is fixed and $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d$, the isomorphism reads
$$D_XLf^*\cong Lf^*D_Y(d)[2d].$$

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal C_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$. Axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum] supplies both adjunctions on these categories, and (A6) supplies $D_T:\mathcal C_T^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\mathcal C_T$ and the natural isomorphisms $\delta_U:U\xrightarrow{\sim}D_TD_TU$. Thus all expressions below remain in the displayed categories. For $U,V\in\mathcal C_T$ use the natural bijection
$$t_T:\operatorname{Hom}_T(U,D_TV)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_T(V,D_TU),\qquad h\longmapsto D_T(h)\circ\delta_V.$$
It is a bijection because full faithfulness of the anti-equivalence first identifies the source with $\operatorname{Hom}_T(D_TD_TV,D_TU)$, and precomposition by the isomorphism $\delta_V$ identifies this with the target. Both identifications are natural by functoriality and naturality of $\delta$. This is a direct use of (A6), not a theorem asserting an ordinary covariant adjunction for $D_T$.

source.place: First sentence: biduality (A6), with variance made explicit

proof.text:
For $A\in\mathcal C_X$ and $B\in\mathcal C_Y$, form the following chain of bijections, natural in both variables:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,D_XLf^*B)
&\xrightarrow{t_X}\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*B,D_XA)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(B,Rf_*D_XA)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(B,D_YRf_!A)\\
&\xrightarrow{t_Y}\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!A,D_YB)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,Rf^!D_YB).
\end{aligned}$$
The second and last arrows are precisely the (A1) adjunctions of [def-sf-datum]. The middle arrow is postcomposition with the inverse of the isomorphism $D_YRf_!A\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*D_XA$ in [thm-sf-verdier-exchange], applicable because $A\in\mathcal C_X$ and the schemes and morphism have its separated finite-type hypotheses. The first and fourth arrows are Step 1. Denote the composite by $\Phi_{A,B}$.

source.place: First sentence through passing to adjoints: explicit Hom-adjunction chain

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] to $\mathcal C_X^{\mathrm{op}}$: with $U=D_XLf^*B$ and $V=Rf^!D_YB$, Step 2 is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,U)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(A,V)$. It gives a unique isomorphism $\chi_{f,B}:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ characterized by $\Phi_{A,B}(h)=\chi_{f,B}\circ h$. Explicitly, $\chi_{f,B}=\Phi_{U,B}(1_U)$, and its inverse is $\Phi_{V,B}^{-1}(1_V)$. Naturality in $A$ shows that both composites are identities. Naturality of $\Phi$ in $B$ shows, for $b:B\to B'$, that
$$Rf^!D_Y(b)\circ\chi_{f,B'}=\chi_{f,B}\circ D_XLf^*(b),$$
which is exactly naturality as functors $\mathcal C_Y^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C_X$.

source.place: Passing to adjoints: representability and the contravariant natural isomorphism

proof.text:
The isomorphism just constructed is the adjoint transform of Verdier exchange: its action on Hom sets is exactly the five-arrow chain of Step 2. Use the identity and composition compatibility of Verdier exchange in clause (6) of [sk-thm-sf-package], with the pasted (A1) units and counits of [def-sf-datum]. The mate-pasting and identity formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identify the adjoint transform of the composite exchange for $gf$ with the composite of the transforms for $f$ and $g$; here the dualities are interpreted as equivalences to opposite categories as in Step 1. In components this says that the Hom transformation for $gf$, after the pullback and exceptional composition comparisons, sends $h:A\to D_XLf^*Lg^*B$ to
$$Rf^!(\chi_{g,B})\circ\chi_{f,Lg^*B}\circ h.$$
The uniqueness characterization in Step 3 therefore gives the asserted formula for $\chi_{gf,B}$. For the identity morphism the identity mate formula gives $h\mapsto h$, so $\chi_{\mathrm{id},B}=1_{D_YB}$. These are compatibility with composition and identities, not an assertion that duality commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Naturally in f: identity and composition of the adjoint transform

proof.text:
Now assume $f$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ and fix the orientation of [def-sf-orientation]. Use the proved smooth purity isomorphism of functors in [sk-thm-purity-transport], rather than inferring purity for arbitrary inputs from the orientation of the coefficient unit. Its hypotheses hold at each of the four coefficient stages in the statement, and (A6) of [def-sf-datum] gives $D_YB\in\mathcal C_Y$. Evaluate that functor isomorphism at $D_YB$ and invert it to obtain
$$Rf^!D_YB\xrightarrow{\gamma_{f,\Lambda}(D_YB)^{-1}}Lf^*D_YB(d)[2d].$$
Composing with $\chi_{f,B}$ gives the second displayed isomorphism. It is natural in $B$ because both factors are natural. The integral operation is completed and the field operations are the rationalized/common-stage ones already specified by the cited purity theorem; no reduction of field coefficients to finite coefficients is used.

source.place: Last sentence: substitute the proved functorial smooth-purity isomorphism

proof_origin.place: Proof, expanded as a variance-correct Hom-adjunction argument; smooth clause uses the existing purity transport theorem

split_report.summary: Repaired contravariant typing and made the implicit domain of absolute duality explicit. Expanded the imported adjoint claim into natural Hom bijections and Yoneda, proved identity/composition using the existing exchange coherence and mate-pasting statements, and used actual functorial smooth purity instead of the unit-orientation definition. A6 is invoked as an axiom of the given datum, so no finite-only geometric biduality theorem is applied at higher coefficient stages. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: The current corollary proof first sentence is Step 1; its adjunction/passing-to-adjoints argument is Steps 2–3; naturally in f is Step 4; its final smooth sentence is Step 5. This is the adjoint Verdier-exchange route of sk-rem-sf-kv-formal, not an external-product or Kunneth argument.

tool_uses.why: The unit explicitly invokes Verdier exchange; its natural isomorphism is the middle arrow of the Hom chain.
